description.narrative: As part of the government's strategy to enhance resilience in the Jordan Valley, particularly in Area C territories, an action plan for value chain development of key agricultural sectors contributing to employment promotion was introduced. Through a collaborative process involving international specialists, tripartite partners and sector stakeholders, the Dairy and Honey sub-sectors in the Jordan Valley were identified as having substantial potential for inclusive growth, entrepreneurship, and the creation of decent employment opportunities, particularly for women and youth. In-depth value chain analyses were conducted for both sectors, and the results were validated through a consultative process. These analyses helped pinpoint key interventions necessary to address constraints that hinder the value chain's ability to contribute to job growth, economic development, and land resiliency. Based on the findings, an action plan was devised in collaboration with the partners to implement measures that promote more effective and secure production practices, establish safe and decent working environments, and enhance overall profitability within the Dairy and Honey sub-sectors. Work by the Palestinian Contractors Union on integrationg Employment Intensive Investment Approaches (EIIP) in the constrcution sector immediately halted following the events of Oct 7th and subsequent ground invasion of Gaza. Prior to the war, the PCU had made progress in introducing EIIP as a mechanism for recovery and to enhance capacities of local stakeholders for a more concerted effort in addressing employment challenges particularly for women and youth in Gaza. Specifically, the PCU led the establishment of a committee to localize the Employment Intensive Investment Approaches (EIIP) component, create training packages, and supervise initiative implementation targeting MSMEs in the construction sector. The ILO commissioned conducting comprehensive Value Chain Analysis (VCA) studies of key sectors in the Jordan Valley, identifying Dairy and Honey sub-sectors as having high potential for inclusive growth, entrepreneurship, and the creation of decent employment opportunities, particularly for women and youth. Detailed analyses of the honey and dairy sub-sectors were completed using several ILO tools and methodologies, including the Global Supply Chain Value Analysis (GSCVA) tool and the methodologies outlined in the ILO’s Value Chain Development for Decent Work Guide, the Guide to Market-Based Livelihood Intervention for Refugees, and Gender-Sensitive Approaches to Value Chain Development: A Complementary Guide. Using ILO tools enabled the value chain analysis to be conducted in line with the ILO’s approaches to promoting decent work and livelihood development. Following a technical review of by ILO specialists, the ILO further facilitated the validation of the results of the VCA and recommendations through stakeholder engagement. Furthermore, the ILO, through local partners, is providing capacity building activities to targeted women to enhance their productivity and business performance, as per the action plan developed. The ILO provided technical support to the PCU to introduce EIIP approaches through offering technical feedback on the adapted training material. In addition, the ILO has provided technical and supervisory support in planning for the implementation of a wide Training of Trainers (TOT) in EIIP.

description.narrative: On February 23rd, 2023, the Palestinian Ministry of Labour successfully convened a Partners’ Meeting to support the implementation of the National Employment Strategy 2021-2025. The meeting received significant backing from international donors and partners, including the ILO, the Arab Labour Organization, and the German Government, with a specific focus on creating gainful employment and job opportunities for Palestinian women, men, and youth. During this Meeting, partners pledged their support to the priorities outlined in the National Employment Strategy, aiming to achieve decent work for all Palestinians. Several bilateral agreements and projects we signed, amounting to a substantial sum of US $40.7 million, between the Ministry of Labour and various international and national partners. These agreements solidified the commitment of these entities to actively contribute to the strategy's successful implementation. With support from the Government of Kuwait, the ILO provided technical and financial support to the NES development process. ILO supported a mapping of existing interventions in each area under the NES and has developed ten thematic fiches based on priority areas in line with the objectives of the Strategy, to guide discussions with development partners and provide a map of investments and efforts ongoing and planned, and the gaps that warrant further funding. Moreover, prior to the donor’s meeting, the ILO assessed current progress of the NES, identifying progress achieved under each one of the themes, as well as financing gaps for priority actions under each.
